idiom_name: duck-typed implementor plus Forwardable or SimpleDelegator
implementation_notes: Ruby has no interfaces: the implementor is any object that responds to the primitive messages, and the abstraction is a class or module holding it, so duck typing plus an explicit delegation declaration replaces the classic abstract Implementor base. Forwardable#def_delegators generates real forwarding methods, which keeps respond_to? honest and the delegated call an ordinary dispatch, while SimpleDelegator forwards everything through method_missing and can change its delegate at runtime with __setobj__. Keep a documented base class that raises NotImplementedError when the contract must be visible to implementors, and prefer a module or a Data class for the primitive side; a delegated call through method_missing costs a full lookup-chain miss.
pitfalls: SimpleDelegator forwards through method_missing and overrides class, so type checks, respond_to? and framework reflection behave unexpectedly and each delegated call pays a lookup-chain miss; Forwardable defines real methods instead.
Hand-rolled method_missing delegation without respond_to_missing? breaks introspection and duck-typing checks elsewhere in the framework.
Duck typing gives no contract: a renamed primitive surfaces as NoMethodError in production, so wrap the implementor boundary with a test or a base class that raises NotImplementedError.
